_comment: Every native payload this library can install, and the only place any of
them is written down. The Kotlin catalogue (NativeArchives.published) is
GENERATED from this file, and the Gradle task that bundles payloads into
the published jar reads the same file — so a digest, a version or a new
platform is edited once and the runtime table, the bundle and the release
cannot disagree about it.
Two hand-maintained copies is how the libass entry went missing for every
platform at once while the archives had been built and published for
months: nothing failed, styled subtitles simply drew nothing.
bundle=true rides inside the published artifact and needs no network at
run time, which is the only arrangement that works for either of these.
libass comes from nomercy-libass, which is private, so a runtime fetch
404s for every consumer. libVLC had no release at all: the URL its digest
named has never existed, there is no system VLC on a stock Windows box,
and the desktop drew a black rectangle with nothing logged.
libass is fetched from its release; libmpv is BUILT at build time by
tools/build-native-payload.sh from the upstream each platform has one of:
the dev package on Windows, Debian's in a container on Linux, Homebrew on
the Mac. Only the macOS payload is host-locked, because a Mach-O
dependency closure needs otool and install_name_tool.
libVLC was here until libmpv replaced it. It is not a fallback that was
kept: an engine nothing constructs is an engine nobody tests, and its
payload was sixty megabytes of plugins.
